decisions.question: Boats now leave the factory with the dual-band radio (our 2 m and 70 cm bands), standing in for a marine VHF set. Should boats get the real marine VHF band instead, as aircraft got the aviation bands?
decisions.context: Radio Framework 0.49.0, the vehicle standard's batch 1 (rows 710, 711). Real boats talk on marine VHF, 156 to 162 MHz. A new band would need a station upgrade and an antenna for it, as the aviation bands do; the dual-band set lets a boat talk to your stations as they are.

options.label: Keep the dual-band set
options.detail: As built: boats talk on our bands, labelled as a simplification; no new station kit.

options.label: Add the marine band
options.detail: A marine VHF band and set for boats, and a station upgrade and mast antennas for it, as for aircraft.

options.label: Both sets
options.detail: A marine set from the factory, and the dual-band set still fittable for talking to hand-helds and convoys.

decisions.why: Boats are few in the owner's game (a dinghy and a trawler) and the dual-band set already lets them talk home; the marine band is a fair later step if boats grow

decisions.question: How strong should the radiation from small nuclear and antimatter blasts be? At one metre a cell, a real mini-nuke's dose would be dangerous across the whole map.
decisions.context: Framework 0.358.0, Patches 0.47.0 (docs/development/radiation-bursts.md, rows 716 to 718). As built, the dose falls the real way (the inverse square and the air), but its scale is squeezed onto a map: IRBM's Mini-Nuke gives about 7 Gy at 50 cells in the open and about 1 Gy at 100. The real 20-ton W54 gave about 100 Gy at 150 m and 5 Gy at 400 m.

options.label: Squeezed onto the map
options.detail: As built: deadly near the blast, sickening for tens of cells beyond it, light further out. Shelter and distance both matter.

options.label: The real scale, as a setting
options.detail: A setting for the real figures: anyone in the open on the map takes a dose that kills; only rock or heavy stone saves them.

options.label: Gentler
options.detail: Half the figures as built: the radiation reaches little past the blast.

decisions.why: It keeps the real shape and makes shelter and distance worth choosing; the real scale would make every small blast a map-wide death sentence, which is what the owner's choice for Legion's strike moved away from

decisions.question: Radiation from other mods' nuclear and antimatter blasts can kill colonists outside the blast. Is it graded moderate (on by default), or high (off until you turn it on)?
decisions.context: The shared design rule: a behaviour that risks the player's people has its own setting, on unless its risk is high or higher. D'thorga Framework's two settings, "Radiation from nuclear blasts" and "Radiation from antimatter blasts", start on.

options.label: Moderate: on by default
options.detail: As built: the player fires most of these weapons, an incoming missile is announced, doses are told in a letter, and shelter and care save people.

options.label: High: off by default
options.detail: New deaths beyond a blast are a whole person lost at once; the player turns it on.

decisions.why: You asked for these weapons' radiation as "in dire need", and the strategic strike's own radiation is on by default

decisions.question: A teacher and a child sitting side by side at the radio terminal: should the lesson count at the radio's rate or the game's full lesson rate?
decisions.context: Built in Radio Framework 0.51.0 (row 722), from your Elmer idea. They now share the terminal's two seats and take no channel, but the lesson still counts at the radio's share (the rules' schoolLessonFactor), as if over the radio.

options.label: The radio's rate
options.detail: As built: sitting together only saves the channel

options.label: The full lesson rate
options.detail: As the game's own lesson, face to face: a reason to send the teacher to the desk

decisions.why: Face to face is a real lesson, and it gives the second seat a purpose of its own; it is no better than the game's own lessons

decisions.question: The live systems schematic for vehicles (the tablet-like page of pipes and cutaways) is a record and a browser mock-up only. Should a first slice be built in the game?
decisions.context: The mock-up is at https://claude.ai/artifact/U1bHEYWoUDudPwcvN9vdQM and the record is docs/development/vehicle-schematic.md. You asked for research and a record only; nothing is built. The sim already keeps most of what the page shows.

options.label: Build a first slice
options.detail: The plain flow sheet for one kind of vehicle: symbols, pipes, state colours, hover and click (SC1, SC3, SC6). No cutaway art yet

options.label: Keep it a record
options.detail: Nothing is built; the mock-up stays as the reference

options.label: Build the whole page
options.detail: Flow sheet, cutaways, tabs and orders together, tested as one piece

decisions.why: It proves the drawing in the game's own windows at little cost, and every later piece sits on it

decisions.question: If the vehicle systems schematic is built, where should the page live?
decisions.context: The mock-up is at https://claude.ai/artifact/U1bHEYWoUDudPwcvN9vdQM and the record is docs/development/vehicle-schematic.md. The Systems tab is 560 by 450; the diagnosis report is 900 by 620.

options.label: Its own window
options.detail: Opened from the Dashboard or the Systems tab; live; hidden in Plain mode as the Systems tab is

options.label: Inside the Systems tab
options.detail: A second view of that tab; no new window, but tight for a cutaway

options.label: In the diagnosis report
options.detail: A mechanic's diagnosis earns the picture; it is a saved report, so it stands still

decisions.why: The picture needs room and its charm is being live; the diagnosis report can reuse the same drawing later

decisions.question: The vehicle systems schematic can be a plain flow sheet made from data for every vehicle, or a drawn engine cutaway for each kind of engine. Which comes first?
decisions.context: The mock-up is at https://claude.ai/artifact/U1bHEYWoUDudPwcvN9vdQM and the record is docs/development/vehicle-schematic.md. The mock-up's 'Drawn as' switch shows both. A flow sheet needs about a dozen white symbols; a cutaway needs one script-drawn picture per kind of engine.

options.label: Flow sheet first
options.detail: Every vehicle gets a page from its loadout; cutaways follow for the engines that earn one

options.label: Cutaways first
options.detail: The turboprop and the diesel as drawn, then more engines; other vehicles wait

options.label: Flow sheet only
options.detail: No cutaways at all: symbols and pipes for everything

decisions.why: 95 vehicle designs carry our systems, so a page from data reaches all of them; the cutaway is the part that takes draughtsmanship

decisions.question: On the vehicle systems schematic, should pipes that carry something show slow drifting marks, or stay still with colour alone?
decisions.context: The mock-up is at https://claude.ai/artifact/U1bHEYWoUDudPwcvN9vdQM and the record is docs/development/vehicle-schematic.md. Its 'Movement' switch shows both. An earlier record set aside animated needles and flashing lamps because a flashing lamp nags; nothing flashes in either form here. You chose to see both before deciding.

options.label: Marks as a preference, off at first
options.detail: Still by default; a display setting turns the drifting marks on

options.label: Still only
options.detail: Colour alone: grey means nothing flows

options.label: Marks always
options.detail: Marks drift wherever something flows and stop with it

decisions.why: On the mock-up, still already reads at once; the marks add direction and life, which is taste

decisions.question: The schematic mock-up draws three parts the mod keeps nothing for: a fuel filter, a chip detector and an inertial separator. Which, if any, are worth building as real behaviours?
decisions.context: The mock-up is at https://claude.ai/artifact/U1bHEYWoUDudPwcvN9vdQM and the record is docs/development/vehicle-schematic.md. Rows M1 to M3. Each would be a new behaviour with its own record: a fuel filter that clogs and is cleared by the engine service; a chip detector that warns of a worn engine before it breaks down; a separator that clogs in dust.

options.label: Chip detector and fuel filter
options.detail: The separator folds into compressor fouling, which already tells the dust story

options.label: None
options.detail: The page draws only what exists; the three are left out

options.label: Chip detector only
options.detail: One early warning the player can act on

options.label: All three
options.detail: Each with its own record first

decisions.why: A chip detector gives a warning the player can act on, and a fuel filter gives fuel quality a place; a clogging separator repeats the compressor wash
